items.title: Q1 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India · Thomas Babington Macaulay
items.stem: When did T. B. Macaulay present his "Minutes on Education" advocating English education in India?
items.explanation: Thomas Babington Macaulay presented his famous 'Minute on Indian Education' to Governor-General Lord William Bentinck on 2nd February, 1835, advocating the promotion of European literature and science through the English medium.

items.title: Q2 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Age of Johnson, Sensibility & Pre-Romantic Transition · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Samuel Johnson, John Dryden, Alexander Pope, Joseph Addison
items.stem:
"It ought to be the first endeavour of a writer to distinguish nature from custom, or that which is established because it is right from that which is right only because it is established; that he may neither violate essential principles by a desire of novelty, nor debar himself from the attainment of beauties within his view by a needless fear of breaking rules which no literary dictator had authority to enact".

The above passage considered to be the death-knell of the neo-classical criticism is attributed to ____.
items.explanation: This passage appears in Samuel Johnson's The Rambler, No. 156 (14 September 1751), where Johnson critiques rigid neoclassical rules such as the dramatic unities and distinguishes universal nature from arbitrary literary custom.

items.title: Q3 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods · Gabriel Garcia Marquez
items.stem: Gabriel Garcia Marquez's postscript to The General in His Labyrinth (1991) about Simon Bolivar's last and terrible journey to the Caribbean coast of Nueva Granada in 1830 is one of the finest examples of _________.
options: reading archive and using its contents.
processing archival information for theoretical judgement.
irrelevance of archive for an artist.
a novelist getting misguided by the archive.
items.explanation: In his 'My Thanks' postscript to The General in His Labyrinth (1989; English trans. 1990), Gabriel García Márquez recounts his exhaustive two-year archival investigation into Simón Bolívar's letters, memoirs, and historical documents, exemplifying how a novelist reads an archive and transforms its contents into fiction.

items.title: Q4 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method of data analysis?
items.explanation: In research methodology, data analysis is systematically categorized into qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods, whereas 'subjective method' is not a recognized scientific method of data analysis.

items.title: Q5 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VII: Cultural Studies · Robert Putnam, Zygmunt Bauman
items.stem: Who has used the term "bowling alone" to describe the erosion of community ties in the United States?
items.explanation: American political scientist Robert D. Putnam coined the phrase 'bowling alone' in his 1995 essay and subsequent book Bowling Alone: The Collapse and Revival of American Community (2000) to analyze the decline of social capital and civic engagement in the United States.

items.title: Q6 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Charles Sanders Peirce
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a kind of 'sign' as suggested by Charles Sanders Peirce?
items.explanation: American pragmatist philosopher Charles Sanders Peirce classified signs in relation to their objects into three fundamental types—Icon, Index, and Symbol—making 'Visual' not one of Peirce's semiotic categories.

items.title: Q7 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods · Paul Thompson, Sylvia Plath, Carolyn Steedman
items.stem: Who among the following was a major advocate of oral history?
items.explanation: British sociologist and historian Paul Thompson is a leading pioneer of oral history methodology, best known for his foundational book The Voice of the Past: Oral History (1978) and for founding the journal Oral History.

items.title: Q8 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Roland Barthes, Northrop Frye, Mikhail Bakhtin, Michel Foucault
items.stem: Who among the following considers a text as a "site of struggle between authority and popular culture"?
items.explanation: Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin, in Rabelais and His World (1965) and The Dialogic Imagination, theorized the novel and carnivalesque folk humor as a dialogic site of struggle between official monologic authority and popular culture.

items.title: Q9 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Restoration Age (Age of Dryden) · Unit II: Poetry · Samuel Butler (17th C)
items.stem: Hudibras of Samuel Butler reflects on the revolt against:
items.explanation: Samuel Butler's mock-heroic verse satire Hudibras (published in three parts in 1663, 1664, and 1678) ridicules the hypocrisy, fanaticism, and pedantry of English Puritans and Presbyterians following the Restoration.

items.title: Q10 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Caroline & Commonwealth / Puritan Interregnum · Unit II: Poetry · Francis Quarles
items.stem: Emblems by Francis Quarles is :
options: A commentary on a volume of Biblical illustrations
A commentary on Thomas More's Utopia
items.explanation: Francis Quarles's Emblems (1635) is a popular seventeenth-century Anglican emblem book consisting of meditative verse paraphrases and commentaries accompanying grotesque and allegorical Biblical engravings.

items.title: Q11 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · Unit II: Poetry · Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, Thomas Sackville, George Gascoigne, Edmund Spenser
items.stem: Who among the following is the author of The Steele Glas ?
items.explanation: Elizabethan poet and dramatist George Gascoigne authored The Steele Glas (1576), one of the earliest English verse satires written in non-dramatic blank verse, contrasting a distorting crystal mirror with an honest steel mirror.

items.title: Q12 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · Unit I: Drama · David Lyndsay
items.stem: Sir David Lyndsay's Satire of the Three Estatis is both
items.explanation: Scottish makar Sir David Lyndsay's morality play Ane Satyre of the Thrie Estaitis (first performed 1540) delivers a trenchant political and religious satire against the corruption of the clergy, nobility, and merchants prior to the Scottish Reformation.

items.title: Q13 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Kamau Brathwaite, Frantz Fanon, Derek Walcott, Ngugi wa Thiong'o
items.stem: Who among the following has used lines from the Shakespearean play Othello to critique racism in one of his poems?
items.explanation: Saint Lucian Nobel laureate Derek Walcott invokes Shakespeare's Othello in poems such as 'Goats and Monkeys' (from The Castaway, 1965) to interrogate racial conflict, blackness, and colonial mimicry.

items.title: Q14 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Derek Walcott
items.stem: Derek Alton Walcott in the poem "The Sea is History" makes a parallel between
options: Evolution of human history and religion
Evolution of Christianity and slavery of the Blacks
items.explanation: In Derek Walcott's poem 'The Sea Is History' (from The Star-Apple Kingdom, 1979), the speaker maps the books of the Judeo-Christian Bible—from Genesis and Exodus to Lamentations and the New Testament—onto the Middle Passage and the history of Black slavery.

items.title: Q15 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: The Age of Chaucer (Ricardian 14th Century) · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · John Mandeville
items.stem: The Voyage and Travail of Sir John Mandeville was written in ___
items.explanation: Originally composed in Anglo-Norman French around 1356–1357, The Voyage and Travail of Sir John Mandeville became a major monument of fourteenth-century Middle English prose through its translation into the Midland dialect.

items.title: Q16 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Age of Johnson, Sensibility & Pre-Romantic Transition · Unit II: Poetry · Thomas Gray
items.stem: "The Elegy written in a Country Churchyard" is written in :
items.explanation: Thomas Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' (1751) is composed in heroic quatrains—four-line stanzas of ten-syllable iambic pentameter lines rhyming ABAB.

items.title: Q17 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Marge Piercy, Shulamith Firestone, Margaret Atwood, Donna Haraway
items.stem: Marge Piercy's novel Woman on the Edge of Time (1976) is based on -
options: Shulamith Firestone's The Dialectic of Sex
items.explanation: Marge Piercy's feminist science-fiction novel Woman on the Edge of Time (1976), depicting the egalitarian, gender-free utopia of Mattapoisett with artificial ectogenesis, draws directly on Shulamith Firestone's radical feminist treatise The Dialectic of Sex (1970).

items.title: Q18 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Geetanjali Shree
items.stem: Which among the following is a short story by the Booker Prize winner Geetanjali Shree:
items.explanation: 'Bel Patra' (included in her 1991 collection Anugoonj) is a short story by International Booker Prize winner Geetanjali Shree, whereas Mai (1993), Hamara Shahar Us Baras (1998), and Khali Jagah (2006) are her novels.

items.title: Q19 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VII: Cultural Studies · Gail Omvedt
items.stem: Women of Palestine (1982) and Indian Women in Struggle (1980) deal with :
options: women's struggle at their work place
items.explanation: Ingela Bendt and James Downing's We Shall Return: Women of Palestine (1982) and Gail Omvedt's We Will Smash This Prison! Indian Women in Struggle (1980) document grassroots female militancy, anti-colonial resistance, and political mobilization.

items.title: Q20 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Arundhati Roy, Kiran Desai, Shashi Tharoor, Rohinton Mistry
items.stem:
The following statement is written by which of the authors given below:
"Could fulfilment ever be felt as deeply as loss?"
items.explanation: The poignant line 'Could fulfillment ever be felt as deeply as loss?' appears at the opening of Chapter 2 in Kiran Desai's Booker Prize-winning novel The Inheritance of Loss (2006).

items.title: Q21 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India · Charles Wilkins, William Jones
items.stem: Who first translated the Bhagavad Gita into English?
items.explanation: British Orientalist Sir Charles Wilkins published The Bhagvat-Geeta, or Dialogues of Kreeshna and Arjoon in 1785 with a preface by Warren Hastings, marking the first direct translation of the Bhagavad Gita from Sanskrit into English.

items.title: Q22 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Restoration Age (Age of Dryden) · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Samuel Pepys, Samuel Johnson, Ben Jonson, Samuel Richardson
items.stem: Who among the following is exclusively associated with diary writing in English?
items.explanation: Restoration naval administrator Samuel Pepys (1633–1703) is famously associated with diary writing in English for his secret shorthand diary kept from 1660 to 1669, recording the Plague, the Great Fire of London, and Restoration life.

items.title: Q23 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit II: Poetry · Matthew Arnold, Robert Browning, Alfred, Lord Tennyson
items.stem: Abt Vogler is authored by
items.explanation: 'Abt Vogler' is a dramatic monologue by Robert Browning published in Dramatis Personae (1864), in which the eighteenth-century German composer and organist extemporizes on his musical instrument and meditates on artistic permanence.

items.title: Q24 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit II: Poetry · Robert Browning
items.stem: The predominant emotion running through the poem "Cristina" by Robert Browning is that of
items.explanation: In Robert Browning's dramatic lyric 'Cristina' (published in Dramatic Lyrics, 1842), the speaker asserts that a single moment of mutual romantic recognition has bound Cristina's soul to his in transcendent, eternal love.

items.title: Q25 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · George Eliot, Emily Bronte, Charles Dickens, Jane Austen
items.stem: Which one is correctly matched?
options: Maggie Tulliver — The Mill on the Floss
items.explanation: Maggie Tulliver is the central protagonist of George Eliot's novel The Mill on the Floss (1860), whereas Heathcliff belongs to Wuthering Heights, Josiah Bounderby to Hard Times, and Fanny Price to Mansfield Park.

items.title: Q26 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Parallel Modernist Tracks: American Modernism, Harlem Renaissance & Indian Gandhian Era · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Ernest Hemingway
items.stem: Which of the following works has Santiago as its protagonist?
options: The Old Man and the Sea
items.explanation: Santiago, an aging Cuban fisherman who struggles with a giant marlin in the Gulf Stream, is the protagonist of Ernest Hemingway's Pulitzer Prize-winning novella The Old Man and the Sea (1952).

items.title: Q27 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Parallel 19th-C Tracks: American Renaissance, Realism & Early Indian English · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
items.stem: Which of the following texts coins the slogan "Vande Matram"?
items.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay composed the hymn 'Vande Mataram' in a blend of Sanskrit and Bengali and included it in his 1882 Bengali historical novel Anandamath, set during the Sannyasi Rebellion.

items.title: Q28 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · W. K. Wimsatt, Roland Barthes, J. Hillis Miller, John Keats
items.stem: Who among the following is associated with the term 'Intentional Fallacy' in literary criticism?
items.explanation: New Critic W. K. Wimsatt, co-writing with philosopher Monroe C. Beardsley, coined the term 'The Intentional Fallacy' (1946, collected in The Verbal Icon, 1954), arguing that an author's intended meaning is external to evaluating a literary work.

items.title: Q29 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: High Modernism, WWI Trench Poets & The 1930s Auden Generation · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Graham Greene, Ernest Hemingway
items.stem: Which of the following works is set in the backdrop of the religious persecution in Mexico?
items.explanation: Graham Greene's novel The Power and the Glory (1940) is set in the Mexican state of Tabasco during the 1930s anti-clerical Calles regime, following a fugitive 'whisky priest' hunted by a socialist lieutenant.

items.title: Q30 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit II: Poetry · F. W. Bateson, F. R. Leavis, J. D. Scott, I. A. Richards
items.stem: Who among the following coined the term 'The Movement'?
items.explanation: J. D. Scott, literary editor of The Spectator, coined the term 'The Movement' in an anonymous October 1954 article ('In the Movement') to describe the anti-Romantic, ironic postwar British writers including Philip Larkin, Kingsley Amis, and Donald Davie.

items.title: Q31 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Yasmine Gooneratne, Imtiaz Dharker, Agha Shahid Ali, Eunice de Souza
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Poet) — List II (Poem/Work)
A. Yasmine Gooneratne — I. Postcard from Kashmir
B. Imtiaz Dharker — II. Advice to Women
C. Agha Shahid Ali — III. Postcards from God
D. Eunice de Souza — IV. This Language, This Woman

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - I, B - IV, C - II, D - III
A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II
A - I, B - II, C - III, D - IV
A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
items.explanation: Yasmine Gooneratne wrote the poem 'This Language, This Woman' (A-IV), Imtiaz Dharker published the collection Postcards from God (1994, B-III), Agha Shahid Ali wrote 'Postcard from Kashmir' (1987, C-I), and Eunice de Souza wrote 'Advice to Women' (1994, D-II).

items.title: Q32 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit I: Drama · Dev Virahsawmy, William Shakespeare
items.stem: Dev Virahsawmy's Toufann is an adaptation of Shakespeare's play _____.
items.explanation: Mauritian playwright Dev Virahsawmy's Mauritian Creole play Toufann (1991) is a postcolonial adaptation and reimagining of William Shakespeare's The Tempest.

items.title: Q33 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit I: Drama · Bhasa, Bhavabhuti, Bharavi, Kalidasa
items.stem: Uttararamacharita by _____ is based on Valmiki's Ramayana.
items.explanation: Eighth-century Sanskrit dramatist Bhavabhuti authored the seven-act play Uttararamacharita ('The Later Story of Rama'), dramatizing the final book (Uttara Kanda) of Valmiki's Ramayana from Sita's banishment to her reunion with Rama.

items.title: Q34 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi
items.stem: In Kannada literature, 'Vachana Movement' addressed
items.explanation: The twelfth-century Kannada Vachana movement, led by Virashaiva/Lingayat saint-poets such as Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, and Akka Mahadevi, used vernacular free-verse lyrics to champion progressive values of caste equality, gender justice, and anti-ritualism.

items.title: Q35 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · William Wordsworth, Samuel Taylor Coleridge, Matthew Arnold, T. S. Eliot
items.stem: "Inane gaudiness" is a phrase used in connection with Neo-classicism by _______.
items.explanation: In the 1800 'Preface' to Lyrical Ballads (and the 1798 'Advertisement'), William Wordsworth critiques eighteenth-century neoclassical poetic diction as 'gaudiness and inane phraseology'.

items.title: Q36 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Classical Greece (Attic Age) · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Aristotle, Samuel Johnson, Matthew Arnold, A. C. Bradley
items.stem: Who defined 'Hamartia' as 'tragic flaw'?
items.explanation: Aristotle introduced the concept of hamartia (error of judgment or tragic flaw in the protagonist) in Chapter 13 of his Poetics as the catalyst of the tragic hero's reversal of fortune.

items.title: Q37 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, Homi K. Bhabha, Stuart Hall, Frantz Fanon
items.stem:
The following statement is given by which of the below mentioned critics?
"I was indignant; I demanded an explanation. Nothing happened. I burst apart."
items.explanation: These lines appear in Chapter 5 ('The Fact of Blackness' / 'The Lived Experience of the Black Man') of Martinican psychiatrist and anti-colonial theorist Frantz Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks (1952).

items.title: Q38 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Gaiutra Bahadur
items.stem: Gaiutra Bahadur is a _____ writer.
items.explanation: Gaiutra Bahadur, author of Coolie Woman: The Odyssey of Indenture (2013), is a Guyanese-American journalist and writer born in Guyana who emigrated to the United States as a child.

items.title: Q39 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: High Modernism, WWI Trench Poets & The 1930s Auden Generation · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Hermann Hesse
items.stem: Hermann Hesse's Siddhartha was originally written in _____.
items.explanation: Nobel laureate Hermann Hesse originally wrote his philosophical novel Siddhartha: Eine indische Dichtung in German, publishing it in Berlin in 1922 after his travels and studies in Indian spirituality.

items.title: Q40 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Brij V. Lal
items.stem: Brij V. Lal's Rama's Banishment deals with the history of Fiji of a time period of _______.
items.explanation: Indo-Fijian historian Brij V. Lal edited Rama's Banishment: A Centenary Tribute to the Fiji Indians, 1879–1979 (1979) on the centenary of Girmitiya indenture in Fiji, though the official NTA answer key marked Option 3 (150 years).

items.title: Q41 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Amitav Ghosh, Gabriel Garcia Marquez, Salman Rushdie, Toni Morrison, Raja Rao
items.stem:
Choose the novels that use 'magic realism' as a tool of narration:
A. The Shadow Lines
B. One Hundred Years of Solitude
C. Midnight's Children
D. Beloved
E. Kanthapura

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B, C, D and E only
items.explanation: Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967, B), Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children (1981, C), and Toni Morrison's Beloved (1987, D) are landmark novels of magic realism (Option 2: B, C and D only).

items.title: Q42 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Irvine Welsh, George Mackay Brown
items.stem:
Which of the following are novels of Irvine Welsh?
A. The Acid House
B. Trainspotting
C. Beside The Ocean of Time
D. Filth
E. Maris Belfrage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Trainspotting (1993, B), The Acid House (1994, A), and Filth (1998, D) are major works of fiction by Scottish writer Irvine Welsh, whereas Beside the Ocean of Time (1994, C) is a novel by George Mackay Brown.

items.title: Q43 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Jacques Lacan, Sigmund Freud
items.stem:
Which of these is related exclusively with Jacques Lacan?
A. Real
B. Id
C. Symbolic
D. Ego
E. Imaginary

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Jacques Lacan's tripartite psychoanalytic schema consists of the Real (A), the Symbolic (C), and the Imaginary (E), whereas the Id (B) and Ego (D) belong to Sigmund Freud's structural model; NTA awarded credit for both Option 3 (C and E only) and Option 4 (A and E only).

items.title: Q44 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Parallel Modernist Tracks: American Modernism, Harlem Renaissance & Indian Gandhian Era · Unit I: Drama · Rabindranath Tagore, Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
items.stem:
Which of the following are NOT by Rabindranath Tagore?
A. Visarjan
B. Chandalika
C. Muktadhara
D. Parineeta
E. Punarnava

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Visarjan (1890, A), Muktadhara (1922, C), and Chandalika (1933, B) are plays by Rabindranath Tagore, whereas Parineeta (1914, D) is a Bengali novella by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay and Punarnava (1973, E) is a Hindi novel by Hazari Prasad Dwivedi.

items.title: Q45 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Yann Martel, Kazuo Ishiguro, Anna Burns, Paul Beatty, Kiran Desai
items.stem:
Identify the film/films that were based on Booker winning novels:-
A. Life of Pi
B. The Remains of the Day
C. Milkman
D. The Sellout
E. The Inheritance of Loss

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Ang Lee's Life of Pi (2012, based on Yann Martel's 2002 Booker winner) and James Ivory's The Remains of the Day (1993, based on Kazuo Ishiguro's 1989 Booker winner) are both film adaptations of Booker Prize-winning novels (A and B only).

items.title: Q46 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit II: Poetry · Robert Browning, Robert Langbaum
items.stem:
Identify the correct ones among the following:
A. The dramatic monologue ensures the reciprocal dialogue of the narrator.
B. The nineteenth century poets fully exploited the poetic form of dramatic monologue.
C. The Poetry of Experience by Robert Langbaum outlines a discussion on dramatic monologue.
D. The linguistic pragmatics make the narcissistic speaker of dramatic monologue speak exclusively.
E. The speaker and the listener in the dramatic monologues of Robert Browning share the same pedestal of communication.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Nineteenth-century Victorian poets like Robert Browning and Alfred Tennyson fully exploited the dramatic monologue (B), Robert Langbaum's The Poetry of Experience (1957) is the classic study of the form (C), and the single speaker monopolizes speech while the auditor remains silent (D).

items.title: Q47 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Homi K. Bhabha, Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, Abdul R. JanMohamed, Edward Said, Aime Cesaire
items.stem:
Identify the Postcolonial critics who used the ideas of Lacan, Foucault and Derrida while critiquing 'Euro-centrism'?
A. Homi Bhabha
B. Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak
C. Abdul JanMohamed
D. Edward Said
E. Aimé Césaire

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
items.explanation: High postcolonial theorists Homi K. Bhabha (A), Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak (B), Abdul R. JanMohamed (C), and Edward Said (D) drew heavily on poststructuralist thinkers Jacques Lacan, Michel Foucault, and Jacques Derrida to critique Eurocentrism, whereas Aimé Césaire (E) belonged to the earlier Francophone Négritude generation.

items.title: Q48 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · George Lamming, Ben Okri, Fred D'Aguiar, Wilson Harris, Zulfikar Ghose
items.stem:
Which among the following are correct?
A. George Lamming - Barbados
B. Ben Okri - Nigeria
C. Fred D'Aguiar - Australia
D. Wilson Harris - Guyana
E. Zulfikar Ghose - India

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: George Lamming was born in Barbados (A), Ben Okri in Nigeria (B), and Wilson Harris in Guyana (D), whereas Fred D'Aguiar is British-Guyanese (not Australian) and Zulfikar Ghose is Pakistani-American.

items.title: Q49 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit I: Drama · Kalidasa, Bhavabhuti, Bhasa, Somadeva
items.stem:
Identify the correct pairs:
A. Kalidasa - Amoghavarsha
B. Bhavabhuti - Uttararamacharita
C. Bhasa - Urubhanga
D. Rajashekhara - Rajatarangini
E. Somadeva - Kathasaritsagara

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Bhavabhuti authored Uttararamacharita (B), Bhasa wrote the Sanskrit tragedy Urubhanga (C), and Somadeva compiled the eleventh-century story collection Kathasaritsagara (E), whereas Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana (not Rajashekhara).

items.title: Q50 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Augustan Age (Age of Pope & Swift) · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Alexander Pope
items.stem:
Which of the following statements hold true with respect to Alexander Pope's "Essay on Criticism"?
A. It is "an inquiry into the nature and value of poetry".
B. It presents "a series of generalizations about good taste".
C. It explores the challenges of impartial and just criticism.
D. It underlines the traits of "the good critic".
E. It critically reflects on Plato's rejection of poetry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and E only
items.explanation: Alexander Pope's An Essay on Criticism (1711) presents neoclassical generalizations about good taste and 'Nature methodiz'd' (B), examines the causes of faulty and biased judgment (C), and outlines the moral and intellectual qualities of the ideal critic in Part III (D).

items.title: Q51 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Mikhail Bakhtin
items.stem:
Which of the following are applicable to the term 'Carnival'?
A. It became important through the work of the Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin.
B. It means the way in which popular humour subverts official authority in classical, medieval and renaissance texts and culture.
C. It overturns the established hierarchy and sets up a popular and democratic counter-culture.
D. It brings out the serious elements in literature.
E. It is used as a critical tool for interpretation of poetry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The concept of the 'carnivalesque' was developed by Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin in Rabelais and His World (A) to describe how folk humor and grotesque realism subvert official authority (B) and temporarily overturn social hierarchies to create an egalitarian counter-culture (C).

items.title: Q52 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)

items.stem:
Which of the following are the premises of Postcolonial Criticism?
A. It rejects the claims of universalism made in the canonical Western literature.
B. It foregrounds the questions of cultural difference and diversity as represented in literary texts.
C. It acts on the principles of peaceful co-existence.
D. It celebrates "hybridity" and "Cultural polyvalency".
E. It resists any attempt at homogenization based on race, class and nationality.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
items.explanation: As summarized by Peter Barry in Beginning Theory, postcolonial criticism rejects Eurocentric universalism (A), foregrounds cultural difference and diversity (B), celebrates hybridity and cultural polyvalency (D), and resists homogenization based on race, class, and nationality (E).

items.explanation: Henry Fielding's The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling (1749, D) is a comic and moralistic novel (A) in which young Tom is caught poaching on Squire Western's estate alongside gamekeeper Black George (C), whereas B falsely splits Tom Jones into two people (A, C and D only).

items.title: Q55 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)

Which of the following are true in the context of "Phenomenology"?
A. It is "a form of methodological idealism" which seeks to explore 'human consciousness'.
B. As a philosophical method, it was developed by Edmund Husserl.
C. Martin Heidegger is one of its leading philosophers.
D. Martin Heidegger's approach is "essentialist".
E. Text is considered purely as an embodiment of the author's consciousness.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
A, B, C and E only
items.explanation: Phenomenology, founded by Edmund Husserl (B) and developed by Martin Heidegger (C), explores human consciousness (A) and in Geneva School criticism views the text as an embodiment of the author's consciousness (E), whereas Heidegger's existential approach is anti-essentialist (giving Option 3: A, B, C and E only).

items.title: Q56 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Oodgeroo Noonuccal

The aboriginal Australian poet, Oodgeroo Noonuccal, in her poem "We are Going" examines the impact of colonial conquest on aboriginal Australians with reference to:
A. Loss of 'bora ground'
B. Loss of aboriginal identity
C. Loss of new education
D. Loss of primitive culture

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Australian Aboriginal poet Oodgeroo Noonuccal's (Kath Walker's) 'We Are Going' (1964), colonial dispossession destroys the tribe's sacred 'bora ground' (A), their Aboriginal identity (B), and their ancestral ways of life (D), giving Option 1 (A, B and D only).

items.title: Q57 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Jacques Derrida, Roland Barthes
items.stem:
What are the points of convergence between Derrida and Barthes?
A. Both believe in the endless play in language and literary texts.
B. Both conclude that the meaning of a text is not final.
C. Both construe that language has retrospective power.
D. They believe that no meaning is reliable.
E. They believe that "the relationship between words, meanings and texts are intrinsic to meaning rather than the word itself."

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
items.explanation: Poststructuralist theorists Jacques Derrida and Roland Barthes converge in affirming the endless play of signifiers in texts (A), the non-finality of textual meaning (B), the instability of fixed meaning (D), and the relational nature of signification across words and texts (E).

items.title: Q58 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)

A. Extradiegetic
B. Heterodiegetic
C. Intradiegetic
D. Homodiegetic
E. Interdiegetic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Narrative Discourse (1972), Gérard Genette classifies narrators by narrative level into extradiegetic (A) and intradiegetic (C), and by relationship to the story into heterodiegetic (B) and homodiegetic (D); only 'interdiegetic' (E) is not a Genette term, so NTA accepted Options 1, 2, and 3.

items.title: Q59 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)

items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about Reader Response Criticism?

B. It refutes that the author is the originator of meaning.
C. It sees the reader as a source of meaning.
D. It treats the text as self-sufficient.
E. It appreciates the texts that are historical.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Reader-response criticism rejects the New Critical view of the text as a self-sufficient container of meaning (A) as well as authorial intentionalism (B), positioning the reader as an active producer of meaning (C); NTA awarded credit for Options 1, 2, and 3.

items.title: Q60 · Oct 2022 (Shift 2)

B. Some of its concepts are pre-empted by F. R. Leavis.
C. It distinguishes between literary and scientific usage of language.
D. It encourages an extensive exploration of the contextual and autobiographical background of a literary production.
E. It vouches for a historical analysis of a text.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: New Criticism drew heavily on I. A. Richards's practical criticism and T. S. Eliot's essays (A), shared close-reading affinities with F. R. Leavis (B), and contrasted literary/emotive language with scientific/referential language (C), while rejecting biographical and historical extrinsic approaches (D, E).

B. Mary Ellmann's Thinking About Women
C. Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar's The Madwoman in the Attic
D. Ellen Moers's Literary Women
E. Kate Millett's Sexual Politics

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: As Elaine Showalter notes in 'Towards a Feminist Poetics' (1979), Patricia Meyer Spacks's The Female Imagination (1975, A), Ellen Moers's Literary Women (1976, D), and Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar's The Madwoman in the Attic (1979, C) are foundational texts of gynocriticism (Option 4: A, C and D only), whereas Mary Ellmann (B) and Kate Millett (E) represent feminist critique of male-authored texts.

B. Janice A. Radway's Reading the Romance (1984) is one of the first examples of the use of ethnographic research methodology.
C. It is perceived as an act of uncovering an objective reality.
D. Reading National Geographic (1993) by Catherine A. Lutz and Jane L. Collins makes effective use of ethnographic research method to find out the role of the magazine National Geographic in moulding Americans' awareness of the world beyond the United States.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
items.explanation: Ethnographic literary research examines how actual audiences consume texts in specific social contexts (A, C), exemplified by Janice Radway's Reading the Romance (1984, B) and Catherine Lutz and Jane Collins's Reading National Geographic (1993, D), making Option 4 (A, B, C and D only) correct.

D. Figures based on Association - Chiasmus
E. Figures based on Indirectness - Euphemism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Paronomasia (punning) is a rhetorical figure of sound (A), Zeugma is a syntactic figure of construction (B), and Euphemism is a figure of indirectness (E), whereas Irony is a figure of indirectness/contrast and Chiasmus is a figure of construction, making Option 1 (A, B and E only) correct.

items.stem:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
Such is the matter of imaginative or artistic literature - this transcript, not of mere fact, but of fact in its infinite variety, as modified by human preference in all its infinitely varied forms. It will be good literary art not because it is brilliant or sober, or rich, or impulsive, or severe, but just in proportion as its representation of that sense, that soul fact, is true, verse being only one department of such literature, and imaginative prose, it may be thought, being the special art of the modern world. That imaginative prose should be the special and opportune art of the modern world results from two important facts about the latter: first, the chaotic variety and complexity of its interests, making the intellectual issue, the really master currents of the present time incalculable - a condition of mind little susceptible of the restraint proper to verse form, so that the most characteristic verse of the nineteenth century has been lawless verse; and secondly, an all pervading naturalism, a curiosity about everything whatever as it really is, involving a certain humility of attitude, cognate to what must, after all, be the less ambitious form of literature. And prose thus asserting itself as the special and privileged artistic faculty of the present day, will be, however critics may try to narrow its scope, as varied in its excellence as humanity itself reflecting on the facts of its latest experience - an instrument of many stops, meditative, observant, descriptive, eloquent, analytic, plaintive, fervid.

In the above passage, Walter Horatio Pater's statement, "Imaginative prose should be special" implies
items.explanation: In Walter Pater's essay 'Style' (from Appreciations, 1889), imaginative prose is identified as the special and opportune art of the modern world because of the chaotic variety and intellectual complexities of modern thought.
